slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: Having a firewall is not the same as being protected

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: Almost every business we assess already owns a capable firewall. The box is rarely the issue. What it is running, and who last looked at it, usually is.

slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Firewall vulnerabilities get published, and because these devices sit on the public internet they are scanned and exploited quickly, sometimes within days of an advisory. An unpatched firewall is not a neutral risk, it is an internet-facing door with a known key. Yet firmware updates get deferred because nobody wants to reboot the internet during working hours, and then the deferral becomes permanent.

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: Somebody opened a port temporarily for a supplier in 2021 and it is still open. An any to any rule went in to get a project finished and never came out. Nobody can say which rules are still needed because there is no record of why they were added, so nobody dares remove any of them.

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: The intrusion prevention, web filtering and threat intelligence that make a next-generation firewall worth buying are licensed separately. When those lapse the device carries on passing traffic quite happily with its best features switched off, and nothing tells you.

slots.label: List item 1
slots.default: Firmware patching on a managed schedule

slots.label: List item 2
slots.default: Rule review with a documented reason for each

slots.label: List item 3
slots.default: Intrusion prevention and web filtering kept licensed

slots.label: List item 4
slots.default: Site to site and remote access VPN

slots.label: List item 5
slots.default: Logging retained so incidents can be investigated

slots.label: List item 6
slots.default: Monitoring and alerting on device health
